examples.knowledge_point: Integrating Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula for Cosine
examples.worked_solution:
We can use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\cos^2\theta -\sin^2\theta=\cos 2\theta.
$$

Letting $\theta = 3x$ gives

$$
\cos^2 3x - \sin^2 3x = \cos 6x,
$$

and therefore,

$$
\eqalign{
		{\int} \left(\cos^2 3x - \sin^2 3x\right ) \, \textrm{d}x&=\int  \cos 6x\, \textrm{d}x\
								&=\dfrac{1}{6}\sin6x+ C.\
                                                                
	}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, we use the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Rearranging the above formula, we get

$$
\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=\operatorname{sin}⁡\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-5)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-5)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)-5x+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-5x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
